---
title: "How to load cells features"
---

This guide downloads and loads the **cells-level feature aggregates** across all IBL
insertions: cell tables, log-binned autocorrelograms, peak-channel waveforms,
population coupling (stPC) and spike-triggered LFP (stLFP).

Where [channel features](load-channel-features.qmd) have one row per recording channel,
these have one row per spike-sorted **unit**.

::: {.callout-important}
These aggregates are in a private S3 bucket and need an IBL account — pass a logged-in
`one.api.ONE` instance to every download function.
:::

## S3 layout

```text
aggregates/atlas/projects/{project}/
│
├── df_probe_details.pqt                  one row per insertion
│
└── cells_aggregates/
    ├── clusters.table.pqt                all cells: QC + anatomy + waveform features   (n_cells × ~59)
    ├── clusters_good.table.pqt           QC-passing cells (bitwise_fail == 0)          (n_good × ~61)
    ├── clusters.acgs_log.npy             log-binned ACGs, normalised by spike_count    (n_cells × 128) float16
    ├── acgs_log.times.npy                ACG bin centres, seconds                      (128,) float64
    ├── clusters.waveforms_peak.npy       peak-channel waveform per cell                (n_cells × 128) float16
    ├── clusters_good.stpc.npy            population coupling                           (n_good × 1000) float16
    ├── clusters_good.stlfp.npy           spike-triggered LFP                           (n_good × 250)  float16
    ├── clusters.acgs_3d.npy              firing-rate-decile × log-lag 3D ACG (~3.5 GB) (n_cells × 10 × 201) float16
    ├── acgs_3d.times.npy                 3D-ACG log-time bin centres, ms                (201,) float64
    ├── waveforms.voltage.npy             all neighbourhood traces (~8 GB)              (n_traces × 128) float16
    └── waveforms.table.pqt               pid / cluster_id / abs_channel index          (n_traces × 3)
```

### Row alignment

This is the part to get right — the arrays carry no index of their own:

| array | row-aligned with |
|---|---|
| `clusters.acgs_log.npy`, `clusters.waveforms_peak.npy`, `clusters.acgs_3d.npy` | `clusters.table.pqt` — **all** cells |
| `clusters_good.stpc.npy`, `clusters_good.stlfp.npy` | `clusters_good.table.pqt` — good cells only |

Note that `clusters.acgs_3d.npy` aligns with **all** cells, not just good units, which is
easy to get wrong given its `clusters.` prefix sits beside the `clusters_good.` arrays.

`clusters.acgs_log.npy` values are in **sp/sp** (normalised by `spike_count`); the
long-lag asymptote converges to the firing rate in sp/s. See
[`compute_3d_acgs`](../api/cells.compute_3d_acgs.qmd) for how the 3D ACGs are computed and
how to recompute them on a new dataset.

## Download

```python
from pathlib import Path

from one.api import ONE
import ephysatlas.data

one = ONE(base_url="https://alyx.internationalbrainlab.org")
local_path = Path("/datadisk/ephys-atlas")
project = "ibl_neuropixel_brainwide_01"

# probe details + cells_aggregates/ (~1 GB; waveforms and 3D ACGs excluded)
ephysatlas.data.download_project_data(local_path, project=project, one=one)
```

The large arrays are opt-in, because most analyses do not need them:

```python
# + waveforms.voltage.npy and waveforms.table.pqt  (~8 GB extra)
ephysatlas.data.download_project_data(
    local_path, project=project, one=one, large_files=True
)

# + clusters.acgs_3d.npy and acgs_3d.times.npy  (~3.5 GB extra)
ephysatlas.data.download_project_data(
    local_path, project=project, one=one, acg3d=True
)
```

To fetch only one of the two parts:

```python
ephysatlas.data.download_probe_details(local_path, project=project, one=one)
ephysatlas.data.download_cells_features(local_path, project=project, one=one)

# the same opt-ins apply here
ephysatlas.data.download_cells_features(
    local_path, project=project, one=one, large_files=True, acg3d=True
)
```

## Load

```python
from pathlib import Path

import ephysatlas.data

local_path = Path("/datadisk/ephys-atlas")
project = "ibl_neuropixel_brainwide_01"

r = ephysatlas.data.read_cells_features(local_path / project)

df_cells        = r["df_clusters"]       # all cells      (n_cells × ~59)
df_cells_good   = r["df_clusters_good"]  # good cells     (n_good × ~61)
acgs_log        = r["acgs_log"]          # (n_cells × 128) float32 — sp/sp
acgs_log_times  = r["acgs_log_times"]    # (128,) seconds
waveforms_peak  = r["waveforms_peak"]    # (n_cells × 128) float32
stpc            = r["stpc"]              # (n_good × 1000) float16 memmap
stlfp           = r["stlfp"]             # (n_good × 250)  float16 memmap
```

The optional arrays appear **only if you downloaded them**, so read them with `.get`:

```python
# present only with large_files=True
waveforms    = r.get("waveforms")       # (n_traces × 128) float16 memmap — ~8 GB
df_waveforms = r.get("df_waveforms")    # (n_traces × 3) — pid/cluster_id/abs_channel

# present only with acg3d=True
acgs_3d       = r.get("acgs_3d")        # (n_cells × 10 × 201) float16 memmap — ~3.5 GB
acgs_3d_times = r.get("acgs_3d_times")  # (201,) log-time bin centres, ms
```

The multi-gigabyte arrays are returned as **memmaps**, so slicing reads only what you ask
for and the whole file never enters memory. Avoid whole-array operations on them —
`waveforms.mean()` will try to read all 8 GB.

## Join with probe metadata

```python
df_probes = ephysatlas.data.read_probe_details(local_path / project)
df = df_cells.merge(df_probes, on="pid", how="left")
```

## Select good units

`clusters_good.table.pqt` uses the strict `bitwise_fail == 0` criterion. For a more
permissive selection based on the refractory-period confidence:

```python
import ephysatlas.cells

df_selected = ephysatlas.cells.select_good_units_relaxed_rp(
    df_cells, rp_confidence_threshold=70.0
)
```

To index the good-cell arrays from the all-cell table — needed whenever you have a mask on
`df_clusters` and want the corresponding `stpc` / `stlfp` rows:

```python
import numpy as np

good_pos = np.where(df_cells["bitwise_fail"] == 0)[0]
waveforms_peak_good = waveforms_peak[good_pos]
acgs_log_good = acgs_log[good_pos]
```
